identity.title: Minimax Optimal Strategy for Delayed Observations in Online Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: The paper studies reinforcement learning when the current state is observed only after a random number of time steps.

contributions.claim: It proposes an algorithm combining state-space augmentation with an upper-confidence-bound approach.
For tabular MDPs, it derives a regret upper bound of tilde-O(H sqrt(D_max S A K)), with D_max the maximum delay.
It formulates delayed-observation learning as a special case of MDPs with a known transition component and an unknown structured component, and establishes general results for that setting.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a broader structured-transition MDP framework in which the delayed-observation problem is a special case, with general results stated to be potentially independently useful.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a regret upper bound of tilde-O(H sqrt(D_max S A K)) for tabular MDPs.
The authors report a matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors, which they use to characterize their approach as optimal.
The authors report general analytical results for the structured-transition MDP setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Delayed state observations are introduced as the reinforcement-learning setting of interest.
An algorithm combining augmentation and upper confidence bounds is proposed.
A delay-dependent regret upper bound is derived for tabular MDPs.
A lower bound matching the upper bound up to logarithmic factors is reported.
The problem is embedded in a broader structured-transition MDP framework with general results.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a concrete delayed-observation problem to a broader MDP class with known and unknown structured transition components, then states general results for that class.

lessons.interpretation: This suggests a useful way to expose reusable theory while retaining a clear application anchor.
lessons.application: Frame a specialized learning problem through an explicitly defined broader model, and state which guarantees apply to the specialization versus the general class.
lessons.exception: Avoid broadening the formulation when the abstraction adds no concrete result or obscures the original task.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the precise delay distribution, feedback protocol, algorithm details, or assumptions behind the bounds.
The constants and logarithmic factors hidden by tilde notation are not given.
The abstract does not provide experimental evidence or details for the claimed general results.
